title: Plot - number, direction, status, and the measured area, perimeter, dimensions and aspect ratio
description:
Select a Space and it reads as a plot: a coloured surface in plan, a paper-thin slab in 3D, and its area, perimeter, bounding dimensions and aspect ratio as numbers. Six nodes: Geometry -> Input Properties -> Math Engine -> Output metrics, with a 2D Render node and a 3D Render node alongside - the same shape as road.json.

  IDENTIFYING TYPE is a CLASSIFIER, not a setting: it reads "plot" and is EDITABLE: FALSE because changing it would make the object lie about what it is. It exists so consumers can ask what a space IS without matching on this file's `id`, which breaks the moment the object is renamed. Its partner is "road" on road.json.

  WHAT YOU DECLARE. Status is the one property that travels with the space and is not derived from it, and it is the only EDITABLE field. Number, Direction and Neighbours are carried for downstream consumers; Space outline is EDITABLE: FALSE because it is fed by the wire from the Geometry node, so hand-editing it would put the readout out of step with the canvas.

  WHAT IS MEASURED. Area by the shoelace formula, taken absolute so winding direction cannot flip its sign. Perimeter as the sum of the edge lengths, the ring wrapped so the closing edge is counted once. Dimension X / Y are the BOUNDING BOX, not edge lengths - correct for an L or a T, where no single edge is the overall width. Aspect is greater over smaller, so it reads >= 1 whichever way the space is turned.

  NOTHING SELECTED IS NOT AN ERROR. An outline with fewer than three points falls back to a stub so the row maths stays well formed, and every published figure is gated on that test - the readout shows zeros and no 2D row is filled.

  STATUS IS A SELECT, AND THAT IS FORCED BY THE RENDER NODE. A 2D Render row's colour is a property OF THE ROW: the evaluator reads `p.color` off the row and there is no `valin-<row>-color` endpoint, so a Math Engine - which can only put numbers on a wire - cannot tint a row. What CAN vary is WHICH ROW RECEIVES THE OUTLINE. So the node carries one row per state (Booked red, Sold yellow, Available green), the Math Engine sends the outline to the row whose name matches Status, and the other two are fed an empty list and skipped outright (2D Render drops a row with no geometry). Exactly one colour is ever drawn and two can never stack. Available is the FALLBACK arm rather than an equality test, so a blank or unrecognised status still draws the plot instead of vanishing.

  Adding a state therefore means two edits, not one: a new option on Status, and a matching row plus one `Plot<Name>` line.

  THE 3D RENDER NODE EXTRUDES THE OUTLINE from z = 0 to 0.001 m - thin enough to read as a floor plate rather than a volume, and a real solid so the 3D view can shade it. Status drives the plan surface only.

  THIS FILE'S IDENTITY BLOCK HAS BEEN LOST ONCE ALREADY. Several save paths write a graph back as {version, nodes, edges} and drop every top-level field with it, at which point the object demotes itself to a plain workflow and Import Objects skips it as "not an object definition". The importer now rebuilds the block from the file's SHAPE when it is missing, so the demotion is no longer fatal - but keep `object` here, because it is what carries the real name, category and description rather than a guess from the filename.

  Holes are not subtracted, and the area is the outline's - to wall centrelines if that is how the Space was made.

props.name: Semantics
props.value: residential land parcel, level developable ground, suburban

params.name: Space metrics
params.expr:
# Space metrics from the selected Space's outline. P arrives as [[x, y], ...] in metres,
# local to the flow anchor.

_n = rows(P)
_ok = _n >= 3 ? 1 : 0
# Nothing selected yet, or a degenerate outline: fall back to a 3-point stub so the row maths
# below is always well formed. Every published figure is gated on _ok, so the readout is zeros
# rather than a crash or a phantom shape.
_Q = _ok > 0 ? P : vcat(hcat(0, 0), hcat(0, 0), hcat(0, 0))
_k = rows(_Q)
_x = col(_Q, 0)
_y = col(_Q, 1)

# The same ring shifted by one vertex, wrapping the last back to the first — the partner every
# edge-wise term below needs.
_x2 = vcat(sub(_x, 1, 0, _k - 1, 1), sub(_x, 0, 0, 1, 1))
_y2 = vcat(sub(_y, 1, 0, _k - 1, 1), sub(_y, 0, 0, 1, 1))
_Q2 = vcat(sub(_Q, 1, 0, _k - 1, 2), sub(_Q, 0, 0, 1, 2))

# Shoelace, absolute so winding direction does not flip the sign. Holes are not subtracted:
# this is the outline's area.
area = _ok * abs(sum(_x * _y2 - _x2 * _y)) / 2
perimeter = _ok * sum(len(_Q2 - _Q))

# Bounding box, not the edge lengths — correct for an L or a T, where no single edge is the
# overall width.
dimX = _ok * (max(_x) - min(_x))
dimY = _ok * (max(_y) - min(_y))

# GREATER over SMALLER, so the ratio is >= 1 whichever way the space is turned: a 2 x 7 room
# reads 3.5, not 0.286.
aspect = _ok * max(dimX, dimY) / max(min(dimX, dimY), 1e-9)

# The slab for the 3D row: the outline extruded from z = 0 to 0.001 m. Thin enough to read as a
# floor plate rather than a volume, and it is a real solid so the 3D view can shade it.
Slab = _ok > 0 ? mprism(_Q, 0, 0.001) : zeros(0, 4)

# STATUS -> COLOUR, for the 2D row: Booked -> red, Sold -> yellow, Available -> green.
# A 2D Render row's colour is a property OF THE ROW, not of the geometry: a Math Engine can only
# put numbers on a wire, never a colour, so one row cannot change hue on a condition. Three rows
# can — red, yellow, green — and the switch becomes a question of WHICH ROW GETS THE OUTLINE. The
# chosen row receives _Q and draws the plot; the other two receive an empty list and are skipped
# outright, because 2D Render drops a row with no geometry rather than drawing nothing visible on
# top of it. No two rows are ever filled at once, so exactly one colour is on screen.
# `status` arrives from the select as its option string. Available is the FALLBACK arm rather than
# an equality test, so a blank or unrecognised status still draws the plot instead of vanishing.
# Nothing selected (_ok = 0) fills no row, which keeps the "nothing selected is not an error" rule
# the rest of this engine follows.
_booked = status == 'Booked' ? 1 : 0
_sold = status == 'Sold' ? 1 : 0
PlotBooked = _ok > 0 && _booked > 0 ? _Q : zeros(0, 2)
PlotSold = _ok > 0 && _sold > 0 ? _Q : zeros(0, 2)
PlotAvailable = _ok > 0 && _booked < 1 && _sold < 1 ? _Q : zeros(0, 2)
